newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies fall limit on weak cash.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies fall limit on weak cash.

text.p: CME pork belly futures fell the daily limit of 3.000 cents per lb on continued pressure from weak cash belly prices, traders said. Hog futures followed on spillover pressure, sources said.

At 1054 CDT, July and August pork bellies sank down the limit with July at 79.175 cents a lb and August at 78.425 cents. Other months were 2.050 cent lower to up 0.275 with only March up. Hog futures were 0.975 to 0.100 lower with August off the most at 80.650 cents.
Talk of further weakness in cash bellies kept commercial pressure on pork belly futures, traders said.

Cash bellies hit resistance last week again at the $90 per cwt level and have been falling since. Pit sources cited reports that cash would be down at least another $1 Monday to $83 on slack demand. Some concern was also developing over deliveries in July which start Tuesday, although there were no definite estimates on the amount that will be delivered, they said.

Early sellers in August bellies were E.D.&F. Man and Refco with Dean Witter a later seller, traders said. R.J. O'Brien and LFG sold July. Locals bought on the early scale down but liquidated later on the continued commercial pressure, pit sources said.

Hog futures fell as spillover pressure triggered sell stops. Hogs had also been pressured by concern over the weak tone to wholesale pork prices which have put packer cutout margins deep in the red, traders said.
However, indications pointed to steady to higher cash hog markets again Tuesday due to lighter-than-expected hog marketings following the long holiday weekend, they added.
R.J. O'Brien sold July and August while Rand Financials bought. Rosenthal Collins and Lynn also sold August while ING bought.
In hog options, Refco sold October 70 puts, LFG bought December 78 calls and Term Commodities bought August 77 puts, pit sources added.
